REPORT  
  Roads have an important role in the economic deve lopment of a country. India has a vast road network  of 3.62 
million km. that consists of Expressways, National Highways, State Highways, major district roads, other district roads 
and village roads. The National Highways and the St ate Highways together account for 2,04,000 kms. The  length of 
National Highways network at present is 70,934 kms.  constituting about 2 per cent of the total road ne twork in the 
country and carrying about 40 per cent of the total  traffic across the length and breadth of the count ry. Between 2001-
02 and 2005-06 the number of vehicles had grown at an average pace of 10 per cent per annum and consequently traffic 
on the roads has increased at 7 -10 per cent per an num. The share of roads in total traffic has been g rowing from 13.8 
per cent of freight traffic and 15.4 per cent of th e passenger traffic in 1950-51 to 60 per cent of fr eight traffic and 87.4 
per cent of passenger traffic respectively by the end of 2005-06. 
2.  This unprecedented growth of road traffic, call s for a massive expansion and improvement of the road network in 
the country. This would require a massive infusion of funds supported by efficient mechanisms and trained manpower. 
Historically in India, investments in roads, especi ally highways, were mainly made by the Government b ecause of the 
large volume of resources required, long gestation period of projects, uncertain returns and various a ssociated 
externalities. But in recent times, the private sec tor has been actively involved in the development a nd maintenance of 
the National Highways. 
3.  The Ministry has formulated policy guidelines t o encourage private sector participation in the hig hway sector, 
besides providing several incentives such as tax ex emptions and duty free import of road building equi pment and 
machinery. Model Concession Agreements have also been finalized for major road projects, under PPP model. 
4.  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is basically responsible for the construction and main tenance of 
National Highways (NH), administration of Motor Veh icle Act and Central Motor Vehicles Rules, formulat ion of 
broad policies relating to road transport, environmental issues relating to vehicular movements, automotive norms, etc. 
besides making arrangements for movements of vehicular traffic with neighbouring countries. 
5.  The development and maintenance of National Hig hways are being done on agency basis mainly by the National 
Highways Authority of India (NHAI), State Public Wo rks Departments (PWDs) and the Border Roads Organiz ation. 
Out of the total length of 70,934 km of National Hi ghways, 42,598 km is with the State Public Works De partments 
(State PWDs), 20,666 km with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and 3,892 km with the Bor der Road 
Organization. Remaining 3,778 km is yet to be entrusted to the executing agencies. 
6.  The National Highways have further been classif ied depending upon the width formation. Generally, a lane has a 
width of 3.75 metres in case of single lane and 3.5  metres in case of multi lane National Highways. Th e break-up of 
National Highways in terms of width is as under: 
  Single Lane/Intermediate lane 19,803 km. (28%) 
  Double Lane 38,006 km. (53.5%) 
  Four/Six/Eight Lane 13,125 km. (14%)

10.  The tables above do not reflect a very good perform ance in achieving the financial and physical target s 
except a few. The Committee finds the reasons given  for the savings are of routine nature. For example , one of 
the reasons for saving CRF is non-submission of proposals and non-receipt of utilisation certificates by the State 
Governments. Reasons for these, if provided could h ave been more revealing to the Committee. The State -wise 
details also could have further provided a real pic ture in this regard. Saving of Rs.50 crores due to retendering 
of works of development of National Highways and St ates roads in naxal affected areas which is a sensi tive 
programme is a cause of concern. Efforts should hav e been made for avoiding the problem necessitating re-
tendering. Further an amount of Rs.20 crore meant f or development of Vijaywada-Ranchi National Highway s 
could not be utilized because draft note for solici ting approval of CCI is still under process even af ter one year 
has passed. Another area of major concern is non-ut ilisation of Rs.600 crore under SARDP-NE due to slo w 
progress of work by BRO. The reasons for slow progr ess are not known. There is a saving of Rs.15 crore  in the 
projects of strategic and Border Roads Project due to non-materialization of supply orders and contrac t for 
procurement of Constructional stores and materials.  Here also, reasons are not given. An amount of Rs. 30 
crores for POSCO could not be utilized due to non-r eceipt of utilization certificates from the Governm ent of 
Orissa. Obviously, due to non-utilization of funds the project must be languishing. An amount of Rs.20  crore 
could not be utilized because Mughal Road Project i s being funded directly by the Planning Commission.  If it 
was so, why the allocation was provided in the Budg et? . What is the status of project? Who is monitor ing the 
project? What is the role of Ministry of Road Trans port and Highways in this project? The explanations  given 
for saving by the Ministry are not clear and convin cing. In view of these, the Committee is of the vie w that the 
Ministry should have been more proactive and taken necessary steps on time to ensure that these delays  in 
execution of projects should have been avoided.  
11.  Another pattern the Committee noted is that many ro ad projects are delayed due to delay in obtaining 
necessary clearances including environmental cleara nce. The delays result in cost and time overruns an d the 
non-achievement of the targets which ultimately imp inges upon national growth and development. The 
Committee is of the view that it leaves an impressi on in the minds of public there being a nexus betwe en the 
contractors and the authorities concern to delay th e projects deliberately so that the project cost go es up 

resulting in more profit. The Government of India should take effective steps to tackle such problems existing in 
the process of award of the road projects including  the grant of environmental clearance. The Committe e is 
aware about the steps taken recently such as consti tution of Task Force headed by the Finance Minister  and 
Inter-Ministerial Group, but feels that process of environmental clearance needs to be further streamlined. The 
infrastructure projects including National Highways  are as important as protecting our national habita t. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport should obtain the environmental clearance before 
finalizing or awarding the cost of project, not vice-versa.  
POOR PERFORMANCE OF CONTRACTORS, NEXUS AND DELAYS  
12.  As regards corruption and unholy collusion bet ween contractors and authorities, The Secretary, Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways was candid enough to accept the operation of such a nexus. He also pointed out about the 
agencies where the real problem existed. He said th at there was nothing wrong with contract with the r ules and 
regulation but the real problem was of enforcements . As regards non-performance, blacklisting and puni shments “in 
few cases they (NHAI) have really declared contract ors as non-performers”. He emphasized that although the Minister 
himself was concerned about it, but “need was to vi gorously pursue them and penalize”. He further clar ified that 
“failure was on the part of NHAI or the State Gover nment or our system “Expressing his helplessness to  do anything 
about it the Secretary called upon the Members of the Committee to do something. He said: 
"... it is these areas where you as a Member of Sta nding Committee must come out strongly and must pass some 
law and those fellows should be punished mercilessl y which is not happening. It is a fact. You see how  the 
contractors, the engineers and the consultants join hands and create disputes. We have seen and the Mi nister has 
said that. Even in land acquisition in NHAI project , the Director and the contractors sometimes join h ands 
together and they de1ay. These have been observed. Really the question is, we have to see how we can i mprove 
the system. How we can check the malaise. This is what I would say..." 
13.  When asked about his responsibility, Secretary , Road Transport and Highways submitted that he was  not 
excluding himself. In first stance, he said the per sons on the ground level were mainly responsible fo r this and 
complaints have been received about it, but “these were mainly enforcement issues and ground level iss ues”, Ministry 
had a limitation as these were basically NHAI matters. 
14.  While concluding the discussion on this issue,  Secretary, Road Transport and Highways said:  
“... All of us have to play our roles, right from m y level, down to the Chairman, NHAI, DG and others.  They 
have to play their roles. They must take action wherever something is wrong...” 
15.  The Committee is also aware of the existence of suc h a nexus leading to corruption and delays not only  in 
this sector but in other sectors as well. A substantial portion of our developmental funds is being siphoned off, as 
a result of which, the desired benefits of our sche mes and programmes are not reaching upto the ground  level. 
What worries the Committee most is the general sens e of helplessness in fighting out this unholy nexus  and the 
consequent alarmingly high “delivery leakages”. The  Committee did not find any serious attempt made or  
proposed against such a nexus in the road sector. T he Committee would like to know the steps taken or 
proposed by the Ministry and NHAI in this regard.  
16.  The Committee enquired from the Ministry how m any Projects were delayed due to the poor performan ce of 
contractors. The Ministry replied that the projects  under NHDP had been delayed mainly due to problems  associated 
with land acquisition, shifting of utilities, obtai ning environment, forest and railway clearances, po or performance of 
contractors, law and order problems in some States,  etc. In most cases projects were delayed due to mo re than one 
factor. It was, therefore, not appropriate to single out one reason for delay on projects. 

17.  The Committee notes that apart from land acquisitio n and various clearances, poor performance of 
contractors is another major reason for delay in ro ad projects. Possibility of a nexus between middlem en, bad 
contractors and corrupt officials to delay the proj ects can not be ruled out. Ministry’s officials cou ld not give 
any information about the projects delayed due to p oor performance of contractors, in fact only one co ntractor 
had been blacklisted so far. The Committee recommen ds that the Ministry should compile the information  
regarding non-performing contractors and they should be black listed.

CONSTRUCTION OF 20 KMS OF ROAD PER DAY  
27.  The Government has announced its commitment to  award the construction of 35000 Kms in five years,  which 
works out to 20 Kms per day. Of this around 14,000 km have been awarded and NHAI is required to award 21,000 
Kms over the next 3 years, so as to achieve the obj ective of constructing 7,000 Kms per year (equal to  20 Kms per 
day). 
28.  The Government had constituted Chaturvedi Comm ittee with the objective of resolving the procedura l 
impediments for the expeditious implementation of National Highways Development Project (NHDP). The Chaturvedi 
Committee submitted its recommendations which also included recommendations for the amendments in MCA.  RFQ 
and RFP documents with regard to awarding of the co ntracts in its first report and the same had been a pproved by the 
Government in November, 2009, with the proviso that  the financing plan for 2010-11 onward would be con sidered by 
the Empowered Group of Ministers (EGoM) for further  action, including such changes to the work plan, a s may 
become necessary. 
29.  The EGoM in its first meeting held on 07.12.20 09 granted in-principle approval for the work Plan-II for 2010-11 
for award of projects covering a length of about 12 ,000 km. EGoM has also approved the additional budgetary support 
(ABS) for SARDP-NE and J&K projects as recommended by the Chaturvedi Committee. In the second meeting held 
on 14th December, 2009 the EGoM approved work plans  2010-11 onwards with the stipulation that of the t otal length 
of National Highways (NH) to be developed broadly 6 0% would be taken up on BOT(Toll) basis, 25% on BOT

can still be improved with better inspection, monit oring and coordination between the Ministries, NHAI , States 
Governments and Private agencies. Association of lo cal representatives, particularly those of M.Ps and  M.L.As 
can prove to be quite effective in many ways. (Para 26)  
CONSTRUCTION OF 20 KMS. OF ROAD PER DAY 
  The 20 Kms per day project is the need of the hou r but based on our past experience and the issue 
involved, it appears to be quite an ambitious targe t, particularly in view of the construction of road s just 2 kms 
per day in previous years so far, we are nowhere ne ar this target. Odds are many, especially those rel ating to 
land acquisition and environmental clearances that have acquired graver proportion now. In view of the se 
limitations, the Committee only hopes that achievin g this target would be a difficult task. It is, how ever, happy 
that the Ministry was working with such a huge target before it. (Para 31)  
NATIONAL  HIGHWAYS  AUTHORITY  OF  INDIA 
  The Committee could see that BE last year had to scale down by about 2,000 crores at RE stage, which the 
Committee only hopes would be actually utilized. Increases in BE 2010-11 would be a challenge before the NHAI 
to utilize fully along with additional amount received as remittance of toll receipts. (Para 35)  
  The Committee is very much concerned over the tar dy progress of projects under NHDP. The Committee 
fails to understand the logic behind delay in compl etion of NS and EW corridors even after the lapse o f 
reasonable period. The Committee feels that the NHAI which is having sufficient funds in its coffer is not serious 
in implementing major projects up to its potential.  The Committee is of the opinion that expanding NHD P 
further without completing the NHDP phase I and II even in the extended schedule will not going to yie ld any 
result. The Committee would also like to have the i nformation on the guidelines/policies followed by N HAI on 
rehabilitation of land owners for the land acquired  for road projects. The Committee is of the opinion  that the 
NHAI is not following standard guidelines in the ca se of offering compensation to the landowners in ro ad 
projects. The Committee feels that timely completio n of such mega projects will benefit both the gover nment 
and the road users. The Committee hopes that NHAI will concentrate more on development of roads rather than 
finding venues to fill its coffers. (Para 40)  
REVISED STRATEGY FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL  HIGHWAYS DEVELOPMENT 
PROJECT (NHDP) 
  The Committee hopes that with the implementation of recommendations of the BK Chaturvedi Report on 
the revised strategy for implementation of National  Highways Development Project, this sector should g et the 
required facelift. The NHAI should not shield itsel f behind delays due to land acquisition, environmen tal 
clearance and other contractor related issues for t he completion of NHDP projects. The Committee feels  that 
development of national highways in the country so far has been rather slow. The Committee hopes that 

ambitious projects of NHAI such as six lane highway s and expressways which are the need of the hour to  keep 
pace with the economic growth of the nation and the ever increasing vehicular traffic should be implemented on 
priority rather than keeping them in approval stage for a longer period. (Para 43)  
ROADS  OF  INTER-STATE  CONNECTIVITY  AND  ECONOMIC  IMPORTANCE 
  The Committee noticed that development of roads o f inter-state connectivity and economic importance are 
not getting their due attention they require. The Committee notes that only one project at a cost of Rs. 6.28 crore 
was approved in the year 2009-10 as against 20 projects in the previous year and only 10 projects were approved 
as against 27 under the Inter-State connectivity projects. The Committee feels that the Ministry should expedite 
faster development of these roads as they play a vi tal role in giving connectivity to major national h ighways 
across the country. The Committee hopes that the Mi nistry will give due consideration for the developm ent of 
these roads during 2010-11 so that more projects could be approved and implemented under these heads. 
(Para 47)  
NATIONAL  HIGHWAYS  (ORIGINAL) WORKS 
  The Committee notes that the budgetary provision for National Highways (O) works in 2009-10 (BE) was  
Rs.3359.55 crore, which was substantially increased  to Rs.4359.55 crore at the RE stage, out of which,  an 
amount of Rs.3370.05 crore was expended till 28.2.2010. However, the allocation has been reduced in the annual 
plan 2010-11 by around Rs. 500 crores that has been  fixed at Rs.3,850.10 crore. The Committee wishes t o 
understand the reasons for enhancing the allocation  at RE stage by Rs.I000 crore and allocating much r educed 
amount in the BE 2010-11. The Ministry on their par t should justify the enhancement in allocation at R E stage 
in 2009-10 by spending up to the level of BE level only. The Committee expresses its concern about the  pattern 
of utilization of funds by the Ministry under this head. It appears that the Ministry is more committe d to 
develop national highways under the NHDP and not th e non-NHDP national highways. The Committee feels 
that such approach of the Ministry in maintaining t he Non-NHDP national highways will definitely affec t the 
already beleaguered national highways network adversely. (Para 50)  
  The Committee also notes that the Ministry may sp end around Rs.I000/crore i.e. 25% of the allocation 
during the month of March 2010. The Committee is of the view that the last minute spending of huge amount of 
money at the fag end of the financial year is again st the norms of a healthy fiscal discipline and tra nsparency. It 
should be avoided. Utilization of plan funds should  be evenly spread throughout the year. Otherwise, t he 
monitoring of the spending of the allocation and quality of the roads may be impossible. (Para 51)  
DEVELOPMENT  OF  NA TIONAL  HIGHWAYS  IN  NORTH-EASTERN  REGION 
  The Committee notes that an amount of Rs.1200 cro re was allocated for SARDP-NE during the year 2009-
10 and an amount of Rs.465.70 was expended till 28.2.2010.Total 270 km roads of 2-lane equivalent stan dards 
were constructed. Together with the roads completed  upto the previous year, total of 450 km roads have  been 
completed under SARDP-NE against 1400 km for execution on EPC basis. The Committee finds the reasons that 
funds could not be utilized fully because of slow p rogress of works under implementation by BRO, 
unconvincing. The Committee recommends that the Gov ernment must look into the actual reasons and help 
BRO to do away the obstacles that delay the project s. The Committee hopes that the development of nati onal 
highways between Jakhilabandha to Upper Assam which is pending for environmental clearance will be cleared 
on priority as also the construction of another bridge over Brahmaputra which is also a longstanding demand of 
North-Eastern Region. The Committee also hopes that NHs 51 and 62 which are in a bad shape will also g et due 
attention from the Ministry since these national hi ghways play a vital role in providing connectivity in the 

North-Eastern Region as national highways are lifeline of the people of this region in the absence of proper road 
and air connectivity. The Committee also ask the NH AI to look into the cases of large numbers of toll gates in 
North-East, particularly NH 62 in Meghalaya.  (Para 57)  
SPECIAL PROGRAMME FOR DEVELOPMENT OF ROADS IN THE L EFT WING EXTREMISM (LWE) 
AFFECTED AREAS AND PROGRAMME FOR DEVELOPMENT OF VIJAYAWADA - RANCHI ROAD 
  The Committee notes the steps taken by the Minist ry for developing roads in the naxalite affected ar eas 
covering 33 districts in eight States. The Committee is at a loss to see that the savings of 2/3rd of plan fund Rs.75 
crore allocated for the development of roads in the  naxal affected areas, only Rs.25 crore is likely t o be spent 
during 2009-10. The Committee finds the reasons ret endering of works in the case of Chhattisgarh and d elay in 
approval of works in Andhra Pradesh due to court ca se, quite routine ones. The Committee would like to  know 
the reasons for retendering of the work in Chhattis garh and the steps taken or advice given to the Sta te 
Governments to sort out the problems. This being a very good scheme, the Government should monitor the  
programme on a regular basis to ensure that the fund is utilized and required infrastructure is constructed in all 
the 33 districts. The Committee is of the opinion t hat the Ministry should coordinate with the Ministry of Home 
Affairs for the successful implementation of this project. The State Governments involved may also be consulted 
on a regular basis for the implementation of the projects. (Para 59)  
CENTRAL  ROAD  FUND 
  The Committee feels that increase in accrual to C RF will naturally result in increased allocation of  more 
funds to the States. The Committee hopes that the M inistry should evolve a monitoring mechanism to ens ure 
that funds allocated under this head are judiciously expended. The Committee notes that an amount of Rs.86.56 
crore is likely to remain unutilized during 2009-10  due to lack of proposals for approval or non-recei pt of 
utilization certificate from States/Union Territori es. The Committee feels that delays in the developm ent that 
should take place in a particular year is further d elayed/ postponed for subsequent years just because of the lax 
execution of the projects and programmes. There is always a cost overrun on the delayed projects which  
ultimately affects the public exchequer and national growth. The Committee recommends that Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways should be proactive and take  up the matter with the State Governments concerned  to 
ensure that proposal and utilization certificate are received from there so that funds are released and utilized. 
       (Para 64)  
NON-PLAN BUDGET (2010-11) MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS OF NATIONAL HIGHWAYS 
  The Committee feels that the Ministry would be in  a position to maintain the national highways in go od 
condition with this allocation. The Committee is of  the opinion that national highways in the country require 
timely and planned maintenance and upkeep in view o f overload they bear. The Committee hopes that the 
Ministry will maintain a uniform quality and improv e the capacity of national highways in due course b y 
utilizing the allocated money to the maximum. The C ommittee recommends that those areas which are affe cted 
by Monsoon and hilly areas affected by landslide an d rain need special attention as far as maintenance  and 
repairs of roads are concerned. (Para 67)   
 
  When asked about the quality and safety on the hi ghways in India, Chairman NHAI argued that our cost  
of road construction was only one-fourth of that in Europe and America. He also argued that toll amount the we 
are collecting in India was only one-eighth/tenth o f that in western countries. He perhaps was arguing  that we 
can not but construct only sub international standa rds roads as we don’t spent as much as USA and Euro pean 
countries do. The Committee finds this comparison, both in terms of cost and amount of toll in India a nd other 

countries, in fact fallacious. This argument overlooks the role of locally available material, technology and cheap 
labour for which most of the multi nationals were o ut sourcing these works to India. NHAI should lay m ore 
emphasize on using indigenous techniques, material suitable to our needs and conditions. The Committee agreed 
with him that quality does not come free but wants to know if we are getting best possible quality eve n with the 
limited funds that we are spending. Answer to this, undoubtedly would be in negative. (Para 68) 
 
REFRESHER TRAINING OF DRIVERS IN UNORGANISED SECTOR  AND HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT 
  The Committee is surprised to find that the HRD s ector is not being given due importance by the 
Government. During 2009-10, an amount of Rs.20 crore approved at BE stage was reduced to Rs.10 crore at RE 
stage, out of which only Rs. 4.30 crore is likely to be utilized. (Para 74)  
  The Committee welcomes the setting up of Training  Institutes for Driving and Research in India as th e 
scheme for setting up of Model Driving Training Sch ools sanctioned during the Tenth Five Year Plan has  
already been discontinued. The Committee feels that  training/refresher courses in this unorganized sec tor need 
a greater push from the Government. Need for such training institutes to hone the skills of drivers can hardly be 
over emphasized. The Committee hopes that the amount of Rs.111 crore approved for 2010-11 would be utilized 
fully for this purpose.   (Para 75)  
NATIONAL  HIGHWAYS  ACCIDENT  RELIEF  SERVICE  SCHEME 
  The Committee finds that out of the allocated amo unt of Rs.29.49 crore (RE) in 2009-10, the Ministry  was 
able to spend Rs.13 crore only. The Committee feels that the purchase of cranes and ambulances are not getting 
the desired priority of the Ministry. In view of in creased number of road accidents, the under utiliza tion of 
funds for such a life saving activities can hardly be justified. The Committee feels that the Ministry  should 
provide adequate number of ambulances and the traum a care equipments along the national highways for 
providing much needed emergency medical aids to accidents victims. (Para 78)  
  The Committee also recommends that the toll colle cting plazas may be equipped with sufficient cranes and 
ambulances so that any emergency happening in their  stretch of the road can be attended to immediately . How 
it is to done may be decided by mutual consultations. (Para 79)  
ROAD  SAFETY  EQUIPMENT  AND  POLLUTION  TESTING  AND  CONTROL 
  The Committee feels that enhanced allocation of f unds under this head will further strengthen the 
pollution control in the country. Number of vehicle s is increasing day by day resulting in more chaos and 
pollution on the roads. The Committee is of the opi nion that in addition to provision of pollution tes ting 
equipments, enforcement of tightened PUC norms will  definitely have positive impact on the green earth . 
Further, there is need for creating awareness through print and electronic media on the dangers of pollution due 
to vehicles. School and college students should be sensitized and involved in the campaign by giving t hem 
suitable incentives.   (Para 82)  
NATIONAL  DATA  BASE  NETWORK 
  The Committee notes the performance of the Minist ry in implementing information technology enabled 
system around 14 States and the steps taken to impl ement the same in other States also. The Committee 
observes that India being a leader in Information T echnology in the world, it is strange that our RTOs  are not 
yet fully computerized. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should 
further pursue with States which have not implement ed the Vahan (Registration Certificate) and Sarathi  

(Driving Licence) projects to implement it in a tim ebound manner. The Committee hopes that with the 
allocation of Rs.30 crore in the BE 2010-11, the Ministry could achieve their target during the current fiscal. 
       (Para 86)  
SETTING  UP  OF  INSPECTION  AND  MAINTENANCE  CENTRE 
  The Committee feels that the Ministry is spending  more time in conception of projects rather than 
implementing the same. The Committee would like to know the steps taken by the Ministry in this regard so far. 
The Committee feels that as the country is already overloaded with old vehicles, time has come for set ting up of 
Inspection and Maintenance Centers to maintain uniform emission and safety norms throughout the country. 
       (Para 91)  
STRENGTHENING  PUBLIC  TRANSPORT  SYSTEM  INCLUDING   INTRODUCTION  OF  IT  LIKE 
AUTOMATIC  FARE  COLLECTION  BASED  ON  GPS 
  The Committee is distressed to note the falling s hare of public transport system as percentage of bu ses in 
the total fleet of vehicles has come down from more  than 11 % in 1951 to 1.1 % in 2004. The Committee feels 
that by revamping the public transport systems in t he country, congestion as well as pollution on the roads can 
be reduced drastically. The Committee while welcomi ng the efforts taken by the Ministry in this regard  hopes 
that the Ministry will pursue the issue with more v igour so that the allocated funds do not remain unu tilized or 
under utilized.     (Para 94) 
 
CREATION  OF  NATIONAL  ROAD  SAFETY  BOARD 
  The Committee is surprised to note that the creat ion of National Road Safety Board has been delayed due 
to one reason or the other. The Committee hopes tha t the Ministry will take all the necessary steps so  that this 
Board is constituted very soon. The Committee, howe ver, likes to caution the Ministry over the tendenc y of 
putting retired/serving bureaucrats in such importa nt bodies making them to serve as resting place. Th e 
Committee recommends that the experts in the field should be given place in the Board so that it can s erve the 
purpose for it has been constituted. (Para 96) 
 
DISPUTE  REDRESSAL  MECHANISM 
  The Committee notes that there exist no effective  dispute redressal mechanisms for resolving the problems 
affecting road sector. This leads to unbridled bureaucratic control and scope for manipulation by those elements 
which have connections and links with middlemen and corrupt authorities. (Para 98)  
  The Committee, therefore, recommends that an effe ctive dispute redressal mechanism in the form of 
tribunals or other mechanism for speedy resolution of conflicts may be put in place at the earliest.     (Para 99)  
TOLL  POLICY 
  The Committee feels that the toll policy in perpe tuity is fundamentally wrong and it needs to be rev iewed 
according to the changing situations. The Committee notes that there are instances of collecting tolls  from areas 
where condition of the roads were so poor. There we re also instances that 23 toll plazas being operate d in a 
stretch of 60 kms. of National Highway 62 in Meghalaya. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Rules 
and Regulations regarding collection of toll should  be revisited and brought at par with the modern da y 
requirements of road users instead of keeping it as  an instrument of unjust profiteering by unscrupulo us 
elements.     (Para 101)  

LESS  ALLOCATION  TO  KERALA 
  Another aspect brought before the Committee is th at the State of Kerala is getting less fund allocation and 
National Highway projects though the State is alway s demanding more for funds and new highway projects . 
Many of the highway projects are delayed especially  the project from Kochi to Kollam. Construction of various 
bypasses undertaken by the Government especially th e Kollam, Alleppy and Thrissur by-passes are lying in 
limbo for years together.  (Para 102)  
  The Committee recommends that the Ministry may lo ok into the delay and expedite the completion of th e 
projects.     (Para 103)  
GENERAL  OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE 
  The Committee while examining the demands of the Ministry felt that one of the major impediments in 
implementing road projects whether it is NHDP or no n-NHDP was the absence of an effective coordination  
among different agencies at different level and at various stages of road constructions. The Committee  is of the 
opinion that absence of such a mechanism in road pr ojects causes delay at every stage from conception to final 
operation. Issues like quality of and safety on roads, development and maintenance of national highways, tolling 
policy, land acquisition and role of States, corrup tion such that they need to be taken for further co nsideration 
separately.     (Para 104) 
 
  The Committee also feels that the Ministry should  give adequate importance to road safety as that of  
development of national highways. The Committee fin ds that the Indian roads lack way side amenities to  users. 
The Committee feels that the Ministry should give a mple consideration in this aspect by providing park ing 
facilities, cafeterias and trauma care centers along national highways and strategically important roads. (Para 
105)  
  The Committee hopes that the Ministry would utili ze the allocated funds diligently to the maximum 
possible.     (Para 106)
